chapter: Reel 4: boyhood bands and the drummers he admired
title: UNIA Drum and Bugle Corps, St. Agnes band and the Church of God gig
summary: He became top drummer of the UNIA corps by nine, then played with the UNIA and St. Agnes bands and for Sunday church services.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: ... they had a Drum and Bugle Corps, and every other Sunday, they would have a parade, and so at the age of 8, I joined this Drum and Bugle Corps. We had a drum teacher there, Mr. McCullen, David McCullen, who was an ex army man from World War I that used to teach us all the different drum beats pieces. And I would learn mine by ear, because I didn't know anything about reading any music, and I don't think he knew too much himself about reading music. But anyway, whatever the rhythms he would play on the marches or the rhythms he'd play on the drum, we all would learn it. By the time I was 9 years old, I had worked myself up to be the number one drummer over all of the older boys that was there. And they also had a marching band that was a part of the UNIA, which I joined around about 9 1/2 years old. But there also was another -- in fact, Miami had like, there was a St. Agnes Marching Band, there was a St. Mary's Marching Band, there was a Masonic Marching Band, and the UNIA had a band. And every Sunday there was a parade -- somebody had a parade; either one of the lodges or one of the churches had a funeral or something like that, because back in those days, in Miami, if you didn't have a band at your funeral, you
were a nobody. I mean you had to have a band at your funeral; that meant that you were somebody.

So anyway, every Sunday there was something going on. So I joined the UNIA band, and from there, that's how I got the chance to meet Brother Roberts, because see, he was the musical director of St. Agnes's band which was the number one band around Miami. They used to play for the churches, and almost all of the lodges.
So I joined St. Agnes' band, too, so I was playing with the UNIA band and I also was playing with St. Agnes' band.

And then from there, there was a man that lived a couple of doors down from us that belonged to the Church of God, Mr. Chipman, who played a cello, and he used to play the bass parts in church with the piano, and him on cello, and the people in church would play the tambourine and the bass drum, so that's how I came in -- I used to play the bass drum on Sundays, although I belonged to the Roman Catholic faith, that was my gig on Sunday -- I used to go to the church and play, and I used to get 50¢ for playing there. It'd be like, all day Sunday.

So anyway, we also used to play for the -- when they got baptized, we used to have to march from, like, 5th and Court Corbin and 17th Street to where the church was, to almost Miami Beach where the water was, and that's where they had the Baptisms there, and we used to march back to the church from there.
